tool_args.old_text:
\paragraph{Ablation reveals functional specialization.}
Zeroing instruction-token attention at L1 across all 32 heads does not affect instruction classification ($100\%$ maintained via the residual stream) but \emph{increases} action MLP probe $R^2$ (using 5 demonstrations per task; absolute values are not directly comparable to Table~\ref{tab:rsa_overview} but within-condition comparisons are valid) from $0.256$ to $0.375$ ($\Delta = +0.119$, 95\% CI $[0.065, 0.167]$, $p < 0.0001$; ablating 24 of 25 instruction-dominant heads yields $R^2 = 0.363$, with the one-head difference due to the $\pm 1$ threshold boundary noted above), indicating that instruction-dominant heads redirect attention from image to instruction tokens at the cost of local action encoding.
Deep-layer representations are unaffected ($|\Delta R^2| < 0.01$ at L8 and L13, 95\% CIs spanning zero, $p > 0.1$), confirming that the attention redistribution is confined to L1.
The restriction of this effect to L1, with L8 and L13 unchanged, argues against a probe-level artifact from reduced input dimensionality.
tool_args.new_text:
\paragraph{Ablation reveals functional specialization.}
To test whether L1 instruction-dominant heads causally mediate a capacity trade-off between instruction routing and action encoding, we ablate their attention to instruction tokens and measure downstream action probe $R^2$ using 50 demonstrations per task ($N = 63{,}228$).
Ablating all 24 dominant heads increases action $R^2$ at L1 by $+0.059$ ($p < 0.0001$; baseline $0.557 \to 0.615$), while ablating 8 non-dominant heads (control) yields only $+0.017$ ($p = 0.008$).
The specificity contrast is significant (dominant $-$ control $= +0.042$, $p < 0.0001$), confirming that the capacity trade-off is specific to instruction-routing heads rather than a generic effect of attention removal.
The effect concentrates at L1 (L8: $+0.018$; L13: $\Delta \approx 0$), consistent with the entry-layer routing pattern identified in \S\ref{sec:learned_routing}.

ssh_fetch_file(

) -> ToolResult
    Fetch a remote file's content as raw bytes for dashboard preview.

    Unlike ssh_read_only(), this doesn't truncate to _MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS — it
    caps at max_bytes and returns raw bytes so the caller can decode or
    stream them as-is. Intended for local, server-side dashboard use only.

    Safety:
      - Rejects remote_path with shell metacharacters to avoid injection.
      - Reads via ``head -c <max_bytes>`` so large files don't overwhelm the
        transport.
      - Does NOT follow symlinks outside the server's own filesystem; the
        remote still applies its own permissions.

    Args:
